newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-FINANCE MINISTER SEES LOWER INFLATION.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-FINANCE MINISTER SEES LOWER INFLATION.

text.p: Lithuania's new Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said he sees no pressures on the horizon which could push inflation back up to worrying levels.
The country's inflation rate in 1996 fell steeply to 13.1 percent from 35.7 percent in 1995.
"Our goal is for lower inflation than last year and we will meet this goal," Shemeta told Reuters in an interview.
"Inflation this year will be 10 to 12 percent," he said.
Shemeta said that the only inflationary pressures expected this year were the elimination of VAT exemptions and increases in domestic energy prices.

"The VAT exemptions were removed at the start of the year and energy prices for household consumers will be increased when this heating season ends...those are the only big inflationary pressures we will encounter," he said.
He added that the government's plan to compensate depositors whose savings were devoured by excessive inflation in 1990-91 would not reignite inflation and stall recovery.
The government says the plan will cost three billion litas and will be funded by the sale of state property and enterprises.
"The plan will be implemented gradually, over a three to five year period, and so it will not have an inflationary impact," he said.
"Only proceeds from privatisation will be used...no other sources will be used," Shemeta said, dismissing any notion that the government would resort to printing money to finance the scheme.
